docs_components_intro: Twintrinsic provides a set of accessible, customizable components built with Svelte 5 and Tailwind CSS. Each component is responsive and follows best practices for accessibility.
docs_welcome: Welcome to the Twintrinsic documentation. Twintrinsic is a collection of accessible, customizable components built with Svelte 5 and Tailwind CSS.

util_intro: Twintrinsic ships a small set of shared helper functions used by the Form select family (AutoComplete, Listbox, Combobox) and the group components (TagGroup, ChipGroup). They are re-exported from the package entry point, so you can import them alongside components:
util_intro2: All helpers accept an item plus an optional field name used to derive the label or value when the item is an object. Always pass the field name explicitly when your objects use a custom key — the helpers default to "label" / "value".
util_getitemlabel_body: Derives a display label for an item. Primitives are stringified as-is; objects yield item[labelField], with null/undefined field values collapsing to "". This unifies the former per-component ?.toString() || "" label pattern.
util_getitemvalue_body: Derives a comparison/submission value for an item. Objects yield item[valueField]; primitives pass through unchanged. Falsy primitives ("", 0, false, null, undefined) are intentionally not collapsed — so a numeric option 0 survives selection comparison.
util_dispatchgroupremove_body: Resolves the item at index from the items array and invokes the group's remove/dismiss callback with a CustomEvent whose detail carries '{'item, index'}' . Shared by TagGroup ("dismiss") and ChipGroup ("remove").
util_detectlanguage_body: Heuristically detects a code language from content patterns (HTML, CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript, JSON, YAML, Markdown, Svelte, shell). Used by CodeBlock when no language prop is provided.
util_propstable_body: For rendering component props and events in your own docs, Twintrinsic ships two utility components — PropsTable and EventsTable. They auto-derive their rows from a component module at build time, with an explicit-array fallback. See their dedicated pages for full usage:
theming_intro: Twintrinsic uses CSS variables and Tailwind CSS for theming. You can customize the look and feel of your application by modifying these variables.
theming_color_scales_body: Twintrinsic provides a comprehensive color system with 10 shades for each color scale (50-900). These color scales provide a consistent palette for your application.

theming_contrast_desc: — a WCAG AAA-leaning theme with pure black text on white (or pure white on black), near-black/white borders, and tuned accent scales so colored text and filled buttons keep strong contrast.
theming_cvd_body_1: Three additional themes (plus dark variants, e.g.
theming_cvd_body_2: ) are tuned for the most common color vision deficiencies using the Okabe-Ito blue-orange safe-axis strategy — they never rely on red-vs-green or blue-vs-yellow alone, so status colors stay distinguishable in both light and dark:
theming_cvd_protanopia_desc: — for red-blind users. Success shifts from green to teal (blue-green) and error shifts from red to vermillion-orange; the orange/amber axis stays readable.
theming_cvd_deuteranopia_desc: — for green-blind users. Success shifts to cyan (reads as blue) while error keeps a strong red, which is still visible without the green cone.
theming_cvd_tritanopia_desc: — for blue-yellow blind users. Primary becomes magenta, secondary red-purple, warning moves from yellow to orange, and info shifts from blue to teal; success and error keep green and red.

completion_approach_1: Twintrinsic was developed using various tools and LLMs. The main IDE is
completion_approach_4: as an AI pair programmer. I have also used
completion_approach_5: when I needed to clean up A LOT of code at once, mainly fixing svelte/ts errors that the other LLMs introduced and adding tests. The development process leveraged AI assistance for:
completion_ai_unit_desc: Vitest-based unit tests for component functionality
completion_ai_e2e_desc: Playwright-based end-to-end tests within Storybook stories
completion_manual_2: was invaluable for generating initial code, they generate poor code and build components using old technology, sometimes building full components from scratch where standard HTML components we can use already exist (like a dropdown component). All components are manually reviewed and updated to ensure they use modern web APIs and best practices. This is necessary due to:

completion_key_2: Implementation of modern dialog and popover APIs where applicable
completion_key_4: Refined Tailwind CSS styling with semantic color naming
completion_key_5: Improved TypeScript type safety and JSDoc documentation

dt_intro_1: Displays structured data in a tabular format with sorting, filtering, pagination, row selection, and custom cell templates. Built on semantic HTML
dt_what: A full-featured data grid component that renders tabular data with column headers, sortable columns, text filters, pagination, and selectable rows. Supports custom cell templates for rich content.
dt_when_2: when you need to display a collection of structured records that users will sort, filter, or paginate through — user lists, product catalogs, transaction logs. For simple static tables, use a plain
dt_why_sorting_desc: click column headers to sort; type to filter
dt_why_pagination_desc: handles large datasets without DOM overload
dt_why_selection_desc: single or multi-select with keyboard support
dt_why_templates_desc: render badges, links, or any HTML in cells
dt_impl_4: `content-visibility: auto` on `<tbody>` for large table performance
dt_mistake_1: Don''t use `<div role="table">` — always native `<table>` for semantics
dt_mistake_2: Don''t forget `<th scope="col">` — screen readers need column header associations
dt_responsive_1: Table scrolls horizontally on narrow viewports.
dt_responsive_3: Compact mode reduces row padding for dense layouts.
dt_kb_2: Toggle sort (on header) or selection (on row)
dt_kb_3: Navigate between cells (when cell navigation enabled)
